findings.title: Image missing alt attribute
findings.reason: The leaf.svg image element has no alt attribute, so screen readers have no text alternative to convey the image content.
findings.who_is_affected: Blind users and people who cannot see images rely on alt text to understand visual content.
findings.how_to_fix: Add a descriptive alt attribute that conveys the content of the image, for example: alt="Diagram of a leaf showing cell structure".

findings.title: Chart image alt text is too generic to convey meaning
findings.reason: The stages-chart.svg has alt="chart", which does not describe the two-stage photosynthesis diagram or its data, leaving screen reader users without the information the chart conveys.
findings.who_is_affected: Blind users and people who cannot see images cannot access the informational content of the chart.
findings.how_to_fix: Replace alt="chart" with a description of the chart content, for example: alt="Two-stage photosynthesis diagram: Stage 1 light reaction splits water and releases oxygen; Stage 2 Calvin cycle converts carbon dioxide into sugar."

findings.title: Video element has no captions
findings.reason: The intro.webm video has no track element providing captions, so deaf and hard-of-hearing users cannot access its audio content.
findings.who_is_affected: Deaf and hard-of-hearing users cannot follow spoken content in video without captions.
findings.how_to_fix: Add a captions track: <track kind="captions" src="media/intro.vtt" srclang="en" label="English" default>.

findings.title: Glossary list contains div children instead of li elements
findings.reason: The ul.glossary element contains div children directly, which is invalid HTML. Screen readers rely on proper list semantics to convey the number of items and allow list navigation.
findings.who_is_affected: Screen reader users depend on semantic list markup to understand structure and navigate by list items.
findings.how_to_fix:
Wrap each div in an li element:
  • ...
  • ...
, or replace the divs with li elements directly.

findings.title: Insufficient color contrast on figure caption
findings.reason: The figcaption has white text (#ffffff) on a #7fb3d5 background with a measured contrast ratio of 2.25, well below the required 4.5:1 for normal-sized text.
findings.who_is_affected: People with low vision or color blindness struggle to read text that does not have sufficient contrast against its background.
findings.how_to_fix: Darken the background color or change the text color to achieve at least 4.5:1 contrast. For example, using #1b4f6b as the background color with white text meets the threshold.

findings.title: Viewport meta tag disables user zoom
findings.reason: The viewport meta tag sets user-scalable=no and maximum-scale=1, preventing users from pinch-zooming or browser-zooming the page on mobile devices.
findings.who_is_affected: People with low vision who increase text size in their browser cannot zoom the page when zooming is disabled.
findings.how_to_fix: Remove user-scalable=no and maximum-scale=1: use <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">.

findings.title: Audio plays automatically with no controls
findings.reason: The audio element has autoplay and loop but no controls attribute. The engine flagged that it outputs audio for more than the allowed duration without a pause or volume mechanism.
findings.who_is_affected: Screen reader users are disrupted by auto-playing audio because it competes with their speech output.
findings.how_to_fix: Add the controls attribute so users can pause or mute the audio, or remove the autoplay attribute and let users start playback themselves.

findings.title: Accordion trigger is not keyboard accessible
findings.reason: The accordion trigger div has a click event listener but is not focusable and is not a native interactive element, so keyboard users cannot reach or activate it.
findings.who_is_affected: Keyboard-only users, switch access users, and screen reader users cannot use a mouse and depend entirely on keyboard access.
findings.how_to_fix: Replace the div with a button element, or add role="button" and tabindex="0" and handle Enter and Space key events.

findings.title: Auto-rotating carousel has no pause mechanism
findings.reason: The carousel rotates slides automatically every 3 seconds via setInterval with no pause, stop, or hide control in the HTML or JavaScript, so users cannot stop the movement.
findings.who_is_affected: People with attention disorders and screen reader users are disrupted by auto-moving content they cannot stop.
findings.how_to_fix: Add a pause/play button to the carousel, or stop auto-rotation when the element receives focus, and provide a mechanism to disable the rotation entirely.

findings.title: Positive tabindex causes focus order disruption
findings.reason: The Next lesson link has tabindex="1", placing it at focus position 1 despite being at DOM position 12, so keyboard focus skips all earlier content and lands on this link first.
findings.who_is_affected: Keyboard users become confused when focus jumps unpredictably around the page.
findings.how_to_fix: Remove the tabindex="1" attribute. Rely on natural DOM order for focus sequence.

findings.title: Page title is generic and non-descriptive
findings.reason: The page has <title>Page</title>, which does not describe the topic or purpose of the lesson media page, making it impossible for users to identify the page by its title.
findings.who_is_affected: Screen reader users and keyboard users rely on the page title to identify the page, especially when switching between tabs.
findings.how_to_fix: Update the title to describe the page, for example: <title>Lesson 3: Photosynthesis in pictures and video - OpenClass</title>.

findings.title: Two Read Further links have ambiguous text with no accessible name
findings.reason: The Read Further section has three links all with visible text More. Two of them have no aria-label to distinguish their destination, making it impossible for screen reader users to identify which page they lead to.
findings.who_is_affected: Screen reader users often navigate by listing all links on a page; ambiguous link text makes it impossible to choose the right one.
findings.how_to_fix: Add unique aria-label attributes to each ambiguous link, for example aria-label="More about light reaction" and aria-label="More about Calvin cycle".

findings.title: Indonesian paragraph lacks lang attribute
findings.reason: The paragraph containing the Indonesian sentence Fotosintesis adalah proses tumbuhan membuat makanan dari cahaya. has no lang attribute to identify the language, even though the page default is English.
findings.who_is_affected: Screen reader users hear garbled pronunciation when foreign-language passages lack a lang attribute.
findings.how_to_fix:
Add lang="id" to the paragraph:

Fotosintesis adalah proses tumbuhan membuat makanan dari cahaya.

findings.title: Accordion trigger uses aria-expanded on a div without button role
findings.reason: The div uses aria-expanded="false" but has no role, and aria-expanded is not a permitted attribute on an element with the generic implicit role, making the state information invalid for assistive technologies.
findings.who_is_affected: Screen reader users rely on name, role, and value to understand and interact with every control on the page.
findings.how_to_fix: Add role="button" and tabindex="0" to the div so that aria-expanded is a valid attribute in context, or replace the div with a native button element.

findings.title: iframe has no accessible name
findings.reason: The practice iframe has no title, aria-label, or aria-labelledby attribute, so screen readers cannot describe the purpose of the embedded content to the user.
findings.who_is_affected: Screen reader users rely on an accessible name on frames to understand and navigate embedded content.
findings.how_to_fix: Add a title attribute describing the frame content: title="Practice exercise: Which gas do plants release?"

findings.title: Carousel slide changes are not announced to screen readers
findings.reason: The carousel container has no aria-live, role="status", or role="alert" attribute, so screen readers receive no notification when the visible slide changes every 3 seconds.
findings.who_is_affected: Blind users do not see status messages that appear on screen; without a live region they have no way of knowing the slide content changed.
findings.how_to_fix: Add aria-live="polite" and aria-atomic="true" to the carousel container, or use a dedicated off-screen live region that announces each slide as it becomes visible.

out_of_reach.title: Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded)
out_of_reach.reason: Whether the intro.webm video contains visual information not conveyed in the audio cannot be determined from code inspection alone; it requires watching the video content.

out_of_reach.title: Captions (Live)
out_of_reach.reason: No live streaming content was identified in the diff; if live media is added later this criterion must be evaluated against a running stream.

out_of_reach.title: Audio Description (Prerecorded)
out_of_reach.reason: Determining whether adequate audio description is provided requires watching and listening to the video content, which cannot be done from source code alone.

out_of_reach.title: Reflow
out_of_reach.reason: Checking that all content is accessible without horizontal scrolling at 320 CSS pixels requires rendering the page at that viewport width; this cannot be verified from code alone.

out_of_reach.title: Text Spacing
out_of_reach.reason: Verifying that content remains readable when line-height, letter-spacing, word-spacing, and paragraph spacing are overridden requires live rendering with a browser extension or bookmarklet.

out_of_reach.title: Three Flashes or Below Threshold
out_of_reach.reason: Detecting whether any content flashes more than three times per second requires video analysis tools and cannot be determined from static source code.

out_of_reach.title: Multiple Ways
out_of_reach.reason: Whether more than one way exists to reach the new page depends on the overall site navigation structure across all pages, not a single page diff.
